artworks.title: Galatea
artworks.description: Raphael's fresco in the Villa Farnesina celebrates Galatea in triumph upon a shell-chariot — a Renaissance image of the Nereid drawn from Ovid and the ancient rolls of Nereus' daughters, though the painter's Galatea is the ideal of marine beauty rather than the mourning lover of Acis.

artworks.title: Acis and Galatea
artworks.description: Claude's landscape sets the Sicilian love-story in golden light: Galatea and Acis at ease before Polyphemus' jealousy shatters the idyll. Ovid's narrative — the Nereid who turned her slain beloved into a river — became a favourite theme of seventeenth-century pastoral painting.
